superseded_calls.notes: First, what is present from nature's first institution is called natural. In this sense Estius says that immortality was natural to the first man and death against nature, since man was created immortal at the beginning, that is, free from the necessity of dying.
The English translation inserts the attribution 'Estius says that', which is completely absent from the Latin source text ('dicit immortalitatem fuisse').

English: 'whether or not it is good for nature, suited to it and in keeping with natural appetite' does not match Latin 'sive sit naturae bonum atque conveniens, & naturali appetitui consentaneum, sive non' meaning 'whether it is a good and suitable thing for nature and in agreement with natural desire, or not' – the English reverses the logical structure and omits the contrastive 'sive... sive non' framing.
The translation accurately reflects the Latin source paragraph without adding, dropping, or distorting any doctrinal or grammatical content.
